blocks.text: fall ill and) because of it, people were visiting him for twenty days.[^1]
Hadhrat Ubayd bin Umayr (RA) reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once led them in the Fajr salaah and started reciting Surah Yusuf. However, he started weeping and had to stop when he reached the verse:

blocks.arabic_text: وَابْيَضَّتْ عَيْنٰهُ مِنَ الْحُزْنِ فَهُوَ كَظِيْمٌ
blocks.text: (Referring to Hadhrat Ya'qoob (AS), Allaah says) His eyes had turned white (blind) with sorrow (because of excessive crying) and he was suppressing it (his sorrow) all the time.
Hadhrat Umar (RA) then went into Ruku.[^2]

blocks.narrator: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Shaddaad bin Haad
blocks.text: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Shaddaad bin Haad narrates that even while standing in the last rows of the congregation, he could hear the sobbing of Hadhrat Umar (RA) during the Fajr salaah. Hadhrat Umar (RA) was reciting Surah Yusuf and (because of his excessive weeping, he had to stop when he) reached the verse:

blocks.arabic_text: إِنَّمَآ أَشْكُوْا بَثِّيْ وَحُزْنِيْٓ إِلَى اللّٰهِ
blocks.text: I complain of my sorrow and my grief only to Allaah.[^3]

Hadhrat Hishaam bin Hasan narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) would sometimes recite a verse of the Qur'aan that would choke him (with emotion). He would then weep so much that he would fall down. (Because of weakness) He would then have to stay indoors and people would visit him thinking him to be ill.[^4]

Hadhrat Haani who was the freed slave of Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Affaan (RA) says that whenever Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) stopped at a graveyard, he would weep so much that his beard would get wet. Someone once asked him, "You do not weep when you think of Jannah and Jahannam but weep when you think of the grave?" He replied, "I have heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say, 'The grave is the first stage from amongst the many stages of the Aakhirah. If one is successful there, the later stages are easier. However, if one is unsuccessful there, the later stages will be extremely difficult.'" Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) also added, "I have also heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say that he had never seen a sight more frightening than that of the grave." In his narration, Hadhrat Haani adds that he heard Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) recite the following couplet by a grave (which means): "If you are saved from this (the punishment in the grave), then you are saved from something enormous
If not, then I do not think that you will be saved (from future torment)"[^5]
